data.analysis: Critique: the subjects are usefully separated by pixel scheduling, scalar primary work, and ambient-ray work, but their wins are not presumed composable. T1 already addresses the key shared-RNG hazard. T2 should isolate its two proposed scalar changes before combining them, since they can affect different costs and floating-point accumulation. T3 risks optimizing intersections while scalar sin/cos and square roots remain costly, and the actual ISA build flags are unspecified; compare these costs and avoid relying on unverified instructions. No child results exist to resolve these hypotheses.

revisions.objective: Optimize only the scalar primary-ray/per-pixel path in src/candidate.cpp, leaving the ambient-occlusion ray-generation/intersection kernel, RNG sequence, and thread scheduling unchanged. Measure invariant hoisting and local scalar accumulation/write-once changes separately against the original, then measure their combination; do not assume combined gains are additive. Preserve geometry and all primary samples, and check any rounding changes against the required RMSE and absolute-mean thresholds. Run all official correctness cases and repeated timings at each performance configuration so the result remains useful when considered for integration with the other tracks.
revisions.subject: Isolated scalar primary-ray and pixel-output experiments

revisions.objective: Investigate ambient-ray generation and intersection throughput in src/candidate.cpp while keeping this separate from primary-ray traversal and OpenMP scheduling. Contrast the cost of scalar direction generation (for example, paired sin/cos only if supported by the frozen build) with batched/compiler-vectorized or intrinsic sphere/plane intersections; measure isolated variants before combinations. Preserve the uniform independent sampling distribution, random consumption where possible, all 64 rays per hit, geometry, and hit/root conditions. Do not use early-outs that omit required intersection work or unverified ISA instructions; retain a build-valid fallback if needed and do not inspect the runtime environment. Report correctness and repeated timings for all official configurations, including nsubsamples=3.
revisions.subject: Ambient-ray generation and intersection throughput

data.shared_assumptions: The three research copies edit only src/candidate.cpp; integration must be measured anew, not inferred additive. Preserve the ABI, valid-input behavior, complete RGB output, full primary and ambient sample counts, uniform independent sampling, and the threads ceiling. Evidence so far is only the correct baseline (three runs, mean 3.4961 s, workload unspecified); no child timings or exact SIMD build flags are available.
